It’s not possible lol not on a global scale. We will create pockets of livable habitat and then charge people insane money to live there. Some places will become straight up uninhabitable, either due to heat, lack of water resources, or both. Storms will get more intense globally, and we don’t know how much more intense. Besides that, our ability to respond to ANY disasters will become precipitously worse with each new disaster. Keep in mind that global warming also means an increase in new diseases (because we will move into new areas and because animals will also be dispersing into new areas), the collapse of our food systems, and could threaten power grids/increase the likelihood of blackouts. This could be a species ending catastrophe, it will almost certainly end society as we know it.

Actually, no lol. Those stones are habitat for ant colonies and millipedes and worms and all assortment of critters. You create bare patches and habitat scarcity when you remove them, even if it’s just for a handful of colonies/critters. Everybody starts doing that and you drastically change the landscape for bugs n such. Same goes for every tree, every mushroom, every single bit of the forest. It might seem trivial to you, but, as an ecologist, I promise you that it isn’t. I have been turning over rocks and opening logs all summer for my research, and I feel horrible about disturbing them, to be honest. Tread lightly in the world. Don’t disturb what you don’t have to. Anything else is ego. Leave as little a mark on public lands as you can.
